items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: Human Rights Watch reports that over 320 people have been detained in Senegal since February for "acts against nature," with at least 84 charged based solely on their HIV status. items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c65y: Dozens of masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank during the annual harvest, injuring 12 people including four dual Palestinian-American citizens and a foreign journalist, a BBC team witnessed. Cars and olive trees were set on fire near the village of Abu Falah. The incident is part of a wider surge in settler violence during this year's harvest season.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/1: Researchers found that Israeli spyware firm Candiru carried out a "zero-click" hacking campaign that steals data just from visiting a webpage or refreshing an app, with no clicks needed. In June 2025, 45 devices used by Al Jazeera staff were infected this way. Citizen Lab's investigation flags it as a new global security risk, since such attacks are far harder for victims to detect or prevent.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2: Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write his short story The Blue Fighter, which won the prestigious Caine Prize for African writing on 6 October. Days later, The Atlantic reported that AI-detection software Pangram flagged the story as almost entirely AI-generated, citing common AI writing patterns. The dispute raises doubts about verifying authorship in literary prizes as AI tools spread.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw14: The Vatican released the first photos of Pope Leo XIV since he underwent lung surgery and was diagnosed with lung cancer at Rome's Gemelli Hospital. items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, visiting Beirut, reaffirmed support for Lebanon and called for Israel's withdrawal amid continuing attacks in the country's south. items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Guinea-Bissau's health ministry says it never approved a controversial US-backed hepatitis B study on newborns, championed by RFK Jr., contradicting claims that influenced a Danish ethics committee's approval. The denial highlights rising scrutiny of US-funded vaccine research and questions around consent and oversight in African countries.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvj6: A British father, Joshua Foster, was fined €3,000 after his two-year-old son fell nearly 40 feet from a hotel window in Cyprus and died. Foster had placed the boy on a windowsill to see a waterpark view, believing the window was shut, and lost control of him. He pleaded guilty to causing death through a reckless act; the family called the loss something they will carry forever.

Meta says it is merely consolidating its ad terms, not expanding scraping rights.
